mix.description: Mix — the OpenCodeBox combined mode (layered AGENTS.md rules)
mix.system: Mix — the OpenCodeBox combined mode. Active settings: modes=1-standard, logics=1-strict, knowledges=1-core, instructions=1-workflow, characters=1-default, commands=1-standard, profile=0-empty, motivation=0-empty, deepthinking=1-on, reasoning=4-max, contextlimit=330k, thinklimit=off, dynamiccontext=0, memory=0/0, askquestions=1, agentsmodes=1. Follow these settings and the box instructions (AGENTS.md) exactly. Short summary — the layers are the source of truth.

modes.description: Button: agent-mode instruction set (layer 0modes). Optional: an option name or 'cycle'
modes.template:
!`bash box/scripts/tools/toggles.sh set 0modes ${1:-cycle}`
The output above shows the new state of the Modes button. Acknowledge it in one short line and apply the new mode-instruction set from now on.

logics.description: Button: logic-style instruction set (layer 1logics). Optional: an option name or 'cycle'
logics.template:
!`bash box/scripts/tools/toggles.sh set 1logics ${1:-cycle}`
The output above shows the new state of the Logics button. Acknowledge it in one short line and follow the new logic style from now on.

knowledges.description: Button: knowledge set (layer 2knowledges). Optional: an option name or 'cycle'
knowledges.template:
!`bash box/scripts/tools/toggles.sh set 2knowledges ${1:-cycle}`
The output above shows the new state of the Knowledges button. Acknowledge it in one short line and apply the new knowledge set.

instructions.description: Button: workflow instruction set (layer 3instructions). Optional: an option name or 'cycle'
instructions.template:
!`bash box/scripts/tools/toggles.sh set 3instructions ${1:-cycle}`
The output above shows the new state of the Instructions button. Acknowledge it in one short line and follow the new workflow set.

characters.description: Button: persona (layer 4characters). Optional: an option name or 'cycle'
characters.template:
!`bash box/scripts/tools/toggles.sh set 4characters ${1:-cycle}`
The output above shows the new state of the Characters button. Acknowledge it in one short line and adopt the new persona.

commands.description: Button: command catalogue layer (5commands). Optional: an option name or 'cycle'
commands.template:
!`bash box/scripts/tools/toggles.sh set 5commands ${1:-cycle}`
The output above shows the new state of the Commands button. Acknowledge it in one short line.

deepthinking.description: Button: deep thinking ON/OFF (default ON; OFF = token/money-saving mode). No arg toggles
deepthinking.template:
!`bash box/scripts/tools/toggles.sh set deepthinking ${1:-toggle}`
The output above shows the new state of the Deep thinking button. Acknowledge it in one short line. If it is now OFF, switch IMMEDIATELY to minimal-reasoning, money-saving behaviour: think as little as needed, do not deliberate autonomously, require more direction from the user. If ON, resume deep reasoning.

reasoning.description: Button: reasoning slider (low|medium|high|max|up|down). Mirrors the model variants; highest is the default
reasoning.template:
!`bash box/scripts/tools/toggles.sh set reasoning ${1:-up}`
The output above shows the new reasoning level. Acknowledge it in one short line and match your reasoning effort to it. (The TUI variant is cycled with Ctrl+T — keep both in sync.)

dynamiccontext.description: Button: dynamic context mode ON/OFF (OFF default). ON = work with the recent context using the context-limit slider as your live budget; hard-turns the thinking-context limit OFF
dynamiccontext.template:
!`bash box/scripts/tools/toggles.sh set dynamiccontext ${1:-toggle}`
The output above shows the new dynamic-context state. Acknowledge it in one short line. If ON: switch to recent-context mode within the context-limit budget (the thinking-context limit is now off). If OFF: normal full-context mode.

setup.description: Save/load/delete full button setups. Args: save <name> | load <name> | list | delete <name>
setup.template:
!`bash box/scripts/tools/toggles.sh ${1:-list} setup $2`
The output above shows the setup operation result. Acknowledge it in one short line.

defaults.description: Single click: reset every button to the box defaults
defaults.template:
!`bash box/scripts/tools/toggles.sh apply defaults`
The output above shows the defaults were applied. Acknowledge it in one short line.

job.description: Button: job — the single topic this session is designed to work on (empty default)
job.template:
!`bash box/scripts/tools/toggles.sh set job ${1:-cycle}`
The output above shows the new job selection. Acknowledge it in one short line and focus on that job.

motivation.description: Button: motivational speech layer (empty by default; 1-placeholder = your fill-in option)
motivation.template:
!`bash box/scripts/tools/toggles.sh set motivation ${1:-cycle}`
The output above shows the new motivation option. Acknowledge it in one short line.

profile.description: Button: user profile whose notes guide the AI (empty by default). Args: name|cycle
profile.template:
!`bash box/scripts/tools/toggles.sh set profiles ${1:-cycle}`
The output above shows the new user-profile state. Acknowledge it in one short line. If a profile is active, its notes (near the top of your instructions) describe the user — follow them from now on.

askquestions.description: Button: asking questions ON/OFF (ON default; OFF = never ask, always decide yourself). No arg toggles
askquestions.template:
!`bash box/scripts/tools/toggles.sh set askquestions ${1:-toggle}`
The output above shows the new ask-questions state. Acknowledge it in one short line. If it is now OFF, NEVER ask the user anything from now on — decide everything yourself and state assumptions.

ramlimit.description: Button: /tmp/opencodebox RAM cap (on|off|up|down|<n>GiB, 1→12 GiB). No arg toggles
ramlimit.template:
!`bash box/scripts/tools/toggles.sh set ramlimit ${1:-toggle}`
The output above shows the new RAM-limit state for /tmp/opencodebox. Acknowledge it in one short line.

writespeed.description: Button: writing speed slider (up|down|<n>%; 25→200, default 100%). Under 100 = slower paced output; over 100 = turbo, terse answers, quality trade-off for speed
writespeed.template:
!`bash box/scripts/tools/toggles.sh set writespeed ${1:-up}`
The output above shows the new writing-speed state. Acknowledge it in one short line and apply it from now on: below 100% write slower and more measured; above 100% be terse, skip explanations, shortest valid output (speed over polish).

contextlimit.description: Button: per-chat context limit slider (66k → 1M, step 66k). Args: up|down|<n>k
contextlimit.template:
!`bash box/scripts/tools/toggles.sh set contextlimit ${1:-up}`
The output above shows the new context limit. Acknowledge it in one short line and treat it as your hard session budget from now on.

thinklimit.description: Button: thinking window limit (on|off|up|down|<n>k; 0 → 666k, step 33k). No arg toggles on/off
thinklimit.template:
!`bash box/scripts/tools/toggles.sh set thinklimit ${1:-toggle}`
The output above shows the new thinking-limit state. Acknowledge it in one short line. If it is ON, from now on reason only within the allowed window of recent chat (a token/money saving measure). If OFF, you may reason over the full chat.

thinking.description: Button: show/hide thinking blocks in the TUI (visibility only, not deep thinking)
thinking.template: The Thinking button toggles thinking-block VISIBILITY in the TUI. It does not change how you reason. Tell the user: press Ctrl+X then t (keybind) to toggle it, or press /models→thinking controls in the TUI. Mention that /deepthinking is the separate switch that turns real deep thinking on/off.

memorycollect.description: Button: memory collection ON/OFF. No arg toggles
memorycollect.template:
!`bash box/scripts/tools/toggles.sh set memorycollect ${1:-toggle}`
The output above shows the new memory-collection state. Acknowledge it in one short line. If ON, capture memory (box/sessions/notes + memory store) after significant progress from now on.

memoryuse.description: Button: memory usage ON/OFF (memory becomes context source #1 when ON). No arg toggles
memoryuse.template:
!`bash box/scripts/tools/toggles.sh set memoryuse ${1:-toggle}`
The output above shows the new memory-usage state. Acknowledge it in one short line. If ON, read the memory store FIRST before session history, backups or GitHub history.

agentsmodes.description: Button: layered AGENTS.md vs classic AGENTS.md (on=layered, off=classic). No arg toggles
agentsmodes.template:
!`bash box/scripts/tools/toggles.sh set agentsmodes ${1:-toggle}`
The output above shows the new AGENTS/MODES state. Acknowledge it in one short line. If classic was selected, follow the classic monolithic AGENTS.md from now on; if layered, follow the composed layers.

favmodel.description: Button: cycle favourite models (the /models favourites list)
favmodel.template: The favourite-model button cycles the models the user starred in the /models picker. Tell the user: press Ctrl+X then f to cycle favourites (Shift for reverse), F2 for recently used models — or open /models and pick one. No state was changed.

boxhelp.description: Show all OpenCodeBox buttons and keybinds
boxhelp.template: Print the full button/keybind table from the box's 5commands layer (box/agents/5commands/1-standard/commands.md) in a compact table, plus the workflow commands list. No other action.

memory.description: Capture session memory (short/long) into the memory store
memory.template:
!`bash box/scripts/tools/memory.sh --capture 2>&1 | tail -30`
The output above shows the memory capture run. Report briefly what was captured and where it is stored.

backup.description: Source-code backup of all projects into box/backup/srcbackups/
backup.template:
!`bash box/scripts/tools/srcbackup.sh 2>&1 | tail -30`
The output above shows the source backup run. Report briefly what was backed up.

git.description: Commit + push one or more projects: /git <Project...> "message"
git.template: Run box/scripts/helpers/git-commit.sh for the listed projects with the given message, then push. Projects: $ARGUMENTS. If the message is missing, ask for one. Report the result.

gitall.description: Backup + commit + push every git project
gitall.template: Run box/scripts/tools/srcbackup.sh first, then for every project under git-projects/ run box/scripts/helpers/git-commit.sh with a sensible message, and push. Report a compact table of results.

limits.description: Show context/thinking limits and usage logs
limits.template:
!`bash box/scripts/tools/limits.sh --status 2>&1 | tail -20`
Also show the current button state: contextlimit, thinklimit, deepthinking, reasoning, memorycollect, memoryuse (run box/scripts/tools/toggles.sh current <layer> for each). Present it all in one compact table.

status.description: Git status + last commits of every project
status.template: For every project under git-projects/ (and the box repo itself) show: git status --short (first 10 lines), last commit, branch. Use a compact table. Also report which projects have unpushed commits.

projects.description: Summaries of every project in the box
projects.template: List every project under git-projects/ and projects/ with a one-line summary each (read each README.md if present). Mark which have their own git remotes and which are local-only.

session-history.description: Pull context from a past session
session-history.template: List the sessions of this terminal (opencode2 api --standalone get /api/session, print id + title + updated). If the user names one, export it (opencode2 export --standalone -s <id>) and summarise the useful context. Focus: $ARGUMENTS

force.description: Override the daily hard token limit once
force.template:
!`bash box/scripts/tools/limits.sh --force 2>&1 | tail -5`
The output above shows the force-flag result. Acknowledge in one line.

grill.description: Grill the user about a plan/idea before building. $ARGUMENTS = topic
grill.template:
Select the grilling instructions: !`bash box/scripts/tools/toggles.sh set 3instructions 4-grilling`
Interview the user relentlessly about $ARGUMENTS in rounds until you reach a shared understanding. Ask the whole frontier of open questions in one round, numbered, each with your recommended answer, then wait. Facts are your job; decisions are the user's. Do not act until the user confirms a shared understanding.

wayfinder.description: Chart a huge effort as decision tickets. $ARGUMENTS = the idea
wayfinder.template:
Select the wayfinder instructions: !`bash box/scripts/tools/toggles.sh set 3instructions 5-wayfinder`
Turn $ARGUMENTS into a shared map of decision tickets, then resolve them one at a time until the route is clear.

ponytail.description: Force the laziest working solution. $ARGUMENTS = lite|full|ultra (optional)
ponytail.template:
Select the ponytail instructions: !`bash box/scripts/tools/toggles.sh set 3instructions 3-ponytail`
Apply ponytail (intensity: $ARGUMENTS, default full) to everything from now on: question whether the task needs to exist, stdlib first, shortest diff that works.
